title: FTSE Russell Q3 2026 quarterly IPO review takes effect at the open — recent IPOs enter the Russell US indexes, implemented after the 2026-09-18 close
source: EST: owner-published, re-fetched and re-extracted independently this session. FTSE Russell, "Frequently Asked Questions -- Russell US Equity Indexes", July 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents PDF, ftse-faq-document-russell-us-equity-2026.pdf, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes -- the same byte count the proposing sibling recorded on 2026-09-06, re-fetched here rather than inherited; 19 content streams inflated and text-extracted in-session 2026-09-06, 15,578 printable characters, page footers "Russell US Equity Indexes, July 2026" read back). TWO INDEPENDENT ROWS IN THAT DOCUMENT GIVE THE DATE. (1) Its dated four-column schedule table's "Quarterly IPO September 2026" column reads verbatim: IPO Review Period "1 May 2026 to 31 July 2026", IPO Market Cap cut-off "31 July 2026", Indicative Review Products circulated "21 August 2026", Query Period "21 August 2026 to 4 September 2026", Lock-Down Period (open of) "7 September 2026", Russell US Style Capping Cut-Off Date "9 September 2026", REVIEW EFFECTIVE DATE (OPEN OF) "21 SEPTEMBER 2026", Russell US Style Quarter-end Capping Cut-Off Date "25 September 2026", and Russell US Style Quarter-end Capping Effective Date (open of, if applicable) "30 September 2026". (2) A SECOND, SEPARATE TABLE -- "Quarterly Addition Guidelines" -- states the STANDING RULE rather than one year's dates, and it is what upgrades this entry's provenance: Rank Date "Last working day in January and July" ("31 July 2026" for the third-quarter column), Announce Date "Fourth Friday prior to the effective date (after market close)" ("21 August 2026"), Effective Date "Third Friday of the month" ("21 September 2026"), with the footnote "** After the close on the third Friday of the month." THE IMPLEMENTATION SESSION IS THEREFORE NO LONGER AN INFERENCE, and the proposal's own caveat that it was one is retired: the owner states in its own words that the quarterly IPO trade prints AFTER THE CLOSE ON THE THIRD FRIDAY, which for September 2026 is Friday 2026-09-18 -- the quad-witching expiry already tracked here as opex-2026-09-18 -- with the review effective at the following open, Monday 2026-09-21. The rule reproduces the owner's own published 2026 values for both quarterly legs to the day (announce 20 February / 21 August 2026; third Friday 20 March / 18 September 2026; effective open 23 March / 21 September 2026), which is the internal check on the reading. Filed estimate for the same reason as every Russell entry in this calendar: the confirmed-tier source prefixes have no member for an index owner's own published schedule, and the FAQ table carries the owner's caveat "NOTE: Dates may be subject to change. Clients will be notified of any changes." Proposed by the russell-recon-lockdown-2026-11-30 initial research; canonical file written by this event's own initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-06), which read the single proposal carrying this id (proposals/russell-quarterly-ipo-review-effective-2026-09-21.from-russell-recon-lockdown-2026-11-30.json) in full first and then re-fetched and re-extracted the owner's document rather than inheriting its readings. Ledger: docs/research/events/russell-quarterly-ipo-review-effective-2026-09-21.md. WHAT THIS ENTRY IS: the calendar's only QUARTERLY Russell leg -- the other five Russell entries are all semi-annual reconstitution milestones. The owner runs exactly two quarterly IPO reviews a year (its own FAQ names only a "First-Quarter" and a "Third-Quarter" column; June and December are the reconstitutions), adding IPOs that priced inside the 1 May to 31 July 2026 window, with no cap-tier migration, no style re-scoring of the universe and no float re-weighting. THE INITIAL RESEARCH MEASURED IT AND FOUND NO INDEX-LEVEL EFFECT, which is why impact stays low: the September effective-open slot alone looks like a signal (IWM-SPY -0.31% mean, 15 of 21 negative 2005-2025, sign p=3.92%, and a placebo panel in which no week-shifted slot clears), but the MARCH leg -- the same event, the same owner-published geometry, the same flow mechanic -- runs +0.18% mean at 15 of 21 POSITIVE, and the two legs pooled are 21 of 42 negative at p=56%, a coin flip. The mechanism is present in both legs; the September calendar is present in only one; the result tracks the calendar. Turnover says the same: the announce session shows no relative-volume step (0.94x), and the implementation Friday's surge is a market-wide expiry effect in which IWM participates LESS than SPY (0.92x relative, 8 of 21 above 1.0). Symbols deliberately EMPTY, as with every sibling: the flow is in the individual names entering, an ETF proxy makes the deterministic screen trip on small-cap beta, and no house playbook is index-flow-keyed. Kind sector matches the sibling market-structure flow entries; the enum has no index-flow member and the imperfect fit is named, not fixed from this lane. ONE ADJACENT EVENT WAS PROPOSED FROM THIS RESEARCH and one was deliberately declined, with reasons recorded so a later lane does not re-litigate either. PROPOSED: russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-09-30, published verbatim in the same schedule table and untracked, which lands on the SAME OPEN as the already-tracked sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-09-30 and runs a near-identical conditional concentration test (Russell: 24% single-name / 4.8% weights collectively above 48%; S&P Select Sector: 24% / 4.8% / 50%). DECLINED: the next quarterly leg, whose effective open derives from the same standing rule as 2027-03-22 -- no owner document published this session names a 2027 date, and more to the point this research measured the class as having no index-level effect, so filing further instances would spend board attention on a null. The 2026-09-25 style capping cut-off was likewise not proposed: nothing publishes on it and no shares move on it, the same class of non-event the russell-recon-preliminary-2026-11-13 lane declined.
